ElementDescription: The NDAR Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for research subject
Subject ID how it's defined in lab/project
Date on which the interview/genetic test/sampling/imaging/biospecimen was completed. MM/DD/YYYY
Age in months at the time of the interview/test/sampling/imaging.
Notes: Age is rounded to chronological month. If the research participant is 15-days-old at time of interview, the appropriate value would be 0 months. If the participant is 16-days-old, the value would be 1 month.
M = Male; F = Female; O=Other; NR = Not reported
e.g., Self-Report, Parent Form, Short Form, Revised Version, Other Informant Form

ElementDescription: Did a hobby or activity for fun. How often? (Use: Self-Report version only)
Attended community events (for example, sporting event, theater/cultural event). How often? (Use: Self-Report version only)
Did things in daily life that were interesting to you. How often? (Use: Self-Report version only)
Found entertainment when bored. How often? (Use: Self-Report version only)
Leisure Frequency: Simple sum of 4 items (reals_leisure_s_freq1 through reals_leisure_s_freq4) (Use: Self-Report version only)
Notes: Total Score Range: 0 - 16; Low score value = worse leisure support; high score value = better leisure support; -9=Score missing due to missing items

ElementDescription: Theta value for reals_leisure_s_freq_total (Use: Self-Report version only)
Notes: Low score value = lowest theta; high score value = highest theta

ElementDescription: Standard deviation for reals_leisure_s_freq_total (Use: Self-Report version only)
Notes: Low score value = less variability; high score value = more variability
